mechanism_narrative: The observed upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks, from -62.0 to -39.9, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue into the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, as seen in the t-1w data (-35.1) following a rise from t-2w (-43.9), suggests a return to office work that will boost weekday retail-and-recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next two weeks following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The combined decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 18.6 to 13.7) and increase in TRANSIT mobility (from -58.7 to -48.4) indicates a shift away from home-bound activities and towards public transit use for external engagements, which will drive retail-and-recreation mobility higher.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite concurrent decreases in RESIDENTIAL and increases in TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in PARKS mobility (from -4.9 to -17.7) followed by a slight recovery (-14.3), combined with the general upward trend in other categories, suggests a seasonal shift where outdoor activities become less dominant, diverting leisure spending towards indoor retail and recreation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a recent decline followed by a slight recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, or PARKS mobility significantly increases, contradicting the seasonal shift.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and steady increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -16.0 to -11.4) reflects a baseline return to essential out-of-home activities, providing a stable foundation that will allow discretionary RETAIL_REC to continue its upward trend.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines significantly, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite stable GROCERY_PHARM trends.

mechanism_narrative: The slight dip in WORKPLACES mobility from t-1w (-35.1) to t-0w (-36.1), after a strong recovery, indicates a potential hesitation or minor setback in the return to normal routines, which could temper the growth of RETAIL_REC in the immediate future.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls week-on-week after a period of sustained increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its strong upward trend in the next week, despite the recent dip in WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The strong inverse correlation between RETAIL_REC and RESIDENTIAL mobility, where people spending less time at home directly translates to more time in retail and recreation venues, will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases while RESIDENTIAL mobility also decreases, or RETAIL_REC increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility increases.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across most mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) suggests an underlying policy shift towards easing restrictions, which will continue to facilitate increased retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Multiple mobility categories (e.g., RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) show a significant decline in the next four weeks, indicating a reversal of policy or public behavior.
